result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.random_walk()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Perform a random walk on the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L36268-L36458){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.random_walk( start, steps, mode="out", stuck="return", seed=None, attr_name=None, return_list=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Random walk](/assets/graphs/random-walk.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A directed house-shaped graph walked from A for 6 steps with a fixed seed. Filled badges give each node's positions in the walk, 0 for the start; A and B are visited twice. The card lists the 7 visited nodes, A, B, C, A, B, D, E; edge E to C is unused." width="100%"} Takes a random walk starting from a given node, choosing neighbors uniformly at random at each step. Edge weights are ignored. Can return the visit order as a list of node IDs, or store the position of each node in the walk as a node attribute for visualization. The walk follows edges according to the `mode=` parameter: - `"out"`: follow outgoing edges (the default) - `"in"`: follow incoming edges (reverse direction) - `"all"`: ignore edge directions (treat as undirected) On an undirected graph all three modes behave the same. If the walk reaches a node with no valid neighbors (gets 'stuck'), behavior is controlled by the `stuck=` parameter. Random walks are useful for: - sampling nodes from a large graph in proportion to how well connected they are - generating node sequences for embedding methods such as DeepWalk or Node2Vec - simulating diffusion, browsing, or foraging processes on a network Time complexity: `O(steps)` with `O(degree)` neighbor lookups per step for `mode="out"`; `"in"` and `"all"` scan the adjacency of every node at each step, so they cost `O(n)` per step. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [start]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node where the walk begins, given as an integer node ID or a string label. [steps]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of moves to make. A complete walk visits `steps + 1` nodes, counting the start node. With `steps=0` the walk is just `[start]`. [mode]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["out"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Which edges the walker may follow from each node: `"out"` (default) follows outgoing edges, `"in"` follows incoming edges backwards, and `"all"` follows edges in either direction. Only matters for directed graphs. [stuck]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["return"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : What to do when the walker reaches a node with no edge it can follow under `mode=`. With `"return"` (default), the walk stops there and the partial walk is used. With `"error"`, a `RuntimeError` is raised instead. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same seed on the same graph always produces the same walk. If `None` (default), the walk is seeded from system entropy and differs from call to call. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute that receives each node's position in the walk. If `None` (default), the attribute is called `random_walk_order`. Positions are 0-indexed, so the start node gets `0`. A node visited several times keeps the position of its *last* visit; nodes never visited get no value. Ignored when `return_list=True`. [return_list]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `False` (default), store the positions as a node attribute (see `attr_name=`) and return the graph for method chaining. If `True`, leave node attributes untouched and return the list of visited node IDs. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[list[int], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_list=` is `True`: list of node IDs visited in walk order, of length `steps + 1` (includes the starting node). May be shorter if `stuck="return"` and the walk terminates early. If `return_list=` is `False`: returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `start=` is a label or integer ID that does not exist, `mode=` is not one of `"out"`, `"in"`, `"all"`, or the walk gets stuck and `stuck=` is not `"return"` or `"error"`. [RuntimeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If walk gets stuck and `stuck="error"`. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Random walks are the substrate under an enormous slice of graph algorithms. PageRank and personalized PageRank interpret each score as the stationary probability of a walker biased by teleportation; Node2Vec, DeepWalk, and related graph embeddings feed sampled walks straight into skip-gram; Walktrap community detection reasons about how long walks tend to stay in a community; and countless sketching and sampling routines lean on walk mixing times to bound their guarantees. On directed graphs the `mode=` argument decides which edges the walker can traverse, which is essential when reversibility is not guaranteed. Setting `seed=` locks in reproducibility, and `stuck='return'` lets the walk terminate gracefully at a sink instead of raising. ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a cycle every node has two neighbors, so the walk never gets stuck: a 10-step walk always visits 11 nodes (including the start), and with `seed=` the result is reproducible: ::: {#57ea78f9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_cycle_graph(6) graph.random_walk(1, steps=10, seed=23, return_list=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [1, 2, 3, 2, 1, 6, 5, 6, 1, 2, 1] ``` ::: ::: Instead of returning the list, the walk order can be stored as a node attribute, which is convenient for coloring nodes by when they were visited. Note that a revisited node keeps the position of its most recent visit, so the start node does not show `0` here: ::: {#25d961bd .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_cycle_graph(20) .random_walk(1, steps=100, seed=23) .colorize_node_attrs( node_attr_from="random_walk_order", palette="viridis" ) ) graph.get_node(1).attributes["random_walk_order"] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 92 ``` ::: ::: On a directed graph, `mode=` controls which edges the walk may follow. On a directed 4-cycle with the default `mode="out"` there is only one way forward, so the walk is deterministic: ::: {#6842d98e .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "A")]) ) path = graph.random_walk("A", steps=6, seed=23, return_list=True) [graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in path] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'A', 'B', 'C'] ``` ::: ::: With `mode="all"` the walker ignores direction and can step either way around the cycle: ::: {#2b1f7956 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} path = graph.random_walk("A", steps=6, mode="all", seed=23, return_list=True) [graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in path] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` ['A', 'D', 'A', 'D', 'C', 'B', 'C'] ``` ::: ::: If the walk reaches a node with no outgoing edges, `stuck="return"` (the default) returns the partial walk instead of raising an error. Here the walk stops at `C` after only two of the ten requested steps: ::: {#4b40b00c .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges( [ ("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), # C has no outgoing edges ] ) ) graph.random_walk("A", steps=10, return_list=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` [1, 2, 3] ``` ::: :::
